**Section 2 Task 7 \- Backup and Rollback Evidence**

Before \[promote.py\](http://promote.py) copies a file to the lane, it backs up the current version as the filename and release\_id.bak. That means every backup is marked with a release ID. The transfer is scp over SSH, then the tool logs the SHA-256 checksum.

Rollback is done with my \[rollback.py\](http://rollback.py). It copies the .bak files and re-verifies the SHA-256. For the database, Branden’s script does the pre-migration backup and restore.

rollback.py restores the release-tagged .bak on qa

Omar Gad owns the backup, rollback, and recovery evidence, which are tasks 7-9. End-to-end promotion verification, which was section 3\. Created \[rollback.py\](http://rollback.py), which fixes the gap in the \[promote.py\](http://promote.py) script. **Section 4 Tasks 1, 2, 3 \- Reflection**

Easiest \- promotion was just a source lane, target lane, and file name, which made the flow easy to follow.

Hardest \- coordinating with the team to get VMs up, backup, rollback, and safe failure around one release ID was difficult to manage and keep from breaking.

I learned \-  How to protect a pipeline in production. Promote to QA, test it, and then promote the same release to prod. The released tagged backup also helped document rollback at each step. Also, I learned not to edit QA or prod directly.
